definition: A language with scarce digital text, labeled data, and evaluation benchmarks relative to English.
details: A language with scarce digital text, labeled data, and evaluation benchmarks relative to English. Dialectal Arabic is the instructive case: hundreds of millions of speakers yet low-resource in data terms, because daily language is spoken, not archived.

explainer.lead: A low-resource language has scarce digital text, labeled data, and benchmarks compared with English. High speaker counts do not guarantee resources, as Dialectal Arabic shows.

tiers.eli5: It's like a language spoken by millions every day but rarely written down online, so there's little for a computer to learn from.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on transfer learning, data collection, and targeted benchmarks when building systems for these languages. A pitfall is assuming speaker population equals data availability.
tiers.paperLevel: A language with scarce digital text, labeled data, and evaluation benchmarks relative to English; Dialectal Arabic is an instructive case, with hundreds of millions of speakers yet low-resource in data terms because daily language is spoken, not archived.

explainer.example: Dialectal Arabic has hundreds of millions of speakers but sparse archived text, so models for it need data collection and transfer from higher-resource languages.
